rows.text: Selenia doubles every point of life you gain, and the deck's whole job is to convert lifegain into opponents' life loss. Behind a wall nobody can attack through, that is a slow inevitability — and with two specific enchantments on the battlefield it stops being slow and becomes a loop that ends the game on the spot. Her death trigger is the third angle: a Curse that doubles one opponent's life loss for the rest of the game.

rows.name: Selenia, the Cursed Heart
rows.text: 2/5 flying lifelink, and ALL your lifegain is doubled. Every drain, every extort, every Authority of the Consuls trigger counts twice.
When she dies you Curse an opponent so their life loss doubles too. That is a reason to kill her yourself rather than protect her forever.

rows.name: Gift of Immortality
rows.text: enchant Selenia. Now every time she dies she comes straight back and the Aura reattaches — so with a sacrifice outlet you can hand out a Curse to every opponent, one per turn.

rows.name: Kaya's Ghostform
rows.text: one mana for the same trick once, and it works through exile.

rows.name: Ayli, Eternal Pilgrim
rows.text: the sacrifice outlet, and it gains you life for the toughness of what you eat. At fifty life it also exiles any nonland permanent, repeatedly.

rows.name: Claws of Gix
rows.text: a free sacrifice outlet that also gains life — doubled, of course.

rows.name: Exquisite Blood
rows.text: whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much.

rows.name: Enduring Tenacity
rows.text: whenever you gain life, an opponent loses that much.
Together those two feed each other forever, and the table's life total goes to zero. It is two cards and uses no combat: allowed in Bracket 3, used from turn 6 on.

rows.name: Bloodthirsty Conqueror
rows.text: the second copy of the Exquisite Blood half, on a 5/5 flying deathtoucher. Either one plus Enduring Tenacity closes the game.

rows.name: Aetherflux Reservoir
rows.text: the backup kill. With doubled lifegain this deck passes fifty life quickly, and fifty damage to any target needs no setup at all.

rows.name: Enduring Tenacity
rows.text: even without the loop, every gain is a drain — and it returns as an enchantment when it dies, so removal only half-answers it.

rows.name: Bloodletter of Aclazotz
rows.text: opponents lose double during your turn. Stack it with Selenia's Curse and the numbers get silly.

rows.name: Kambal, Consul of Allocation
rows.text: two off them and two to you on every noncreature spell they cast, doubled to four gained.

rows.name: Liesa, Shroud of Dusk
rows.text: two life from every player on every spell, and her commander tax is paid in life rather than mana.

rows.name: Blind Obedience
rows.text: extort on every spell you cast, plus their creatures and artifacts enter tapped.

rows.name: Debt to the Deathless
rows.text: the clean X finisher — two times X from each opponent, and you gain all of it back doubled.

rows.name: Fraying Omnipotence
rows.text: everyone halves their life, hand and board. You are the player who can afford it, and the life loss is doubled by any Curse out.

rows.name: Authority of the Consuls
rows.text: a life every time any opponent plays a creature, and their creatures arrive tapped so nothing has haste.

rows.name: Haliya, Guided by Light
rows.text: a life for every creature or artifact you play, and a card at end step whenever you gained three.

rows.name: Exemplar of Light
rows.text: a counter for every lifegain event and a card each turn it grows.

rows.name: Archivist of Oghma
rows.text: a card and a life every time anyone searches their library.

rows.name: Ayli, Eternal Pilgrim
rows.text: life equal to whatever you sacrifice.

rows.name: Black Market Connections
rows.text: three effects a turn, paid in life you are gaining back at double rate.

rows.name: Necropotence
rows.text: as many cards as you want, and this deck's life total is not the constraint it usually is.

rows.name: Moat
rows.text: creatures without flying cannot attack. Selenia flies; most of the table does not.

rows.name: Ghostly Prison
rows.text: taxes what Moat does not stop.

rows.name: Authority of the Consuls
rows.text: no haste kills, no surprise blockers.

rows.name: Blind Obedience
rows.text: the same for artifacts.

rows.name: Archon of Emeria
rows.text: one spell per turn each, and their nonbasics enter tapped.

rows.name: Grand Abolisher
rows.text: nobody interacts during your turn — cast this before you go for the loop.

rows.name: Inkshield
rows.text: prevents a lethal alpha strike and converts it into a flying army.

rows.name: Clever Concealment
rows.text: usually free with convoke, and it phases your whole board out of a wrath.

rows.name: Anguished Unmaking
rows.text: instant-speed exile for any nonland permanent.

rows.name: Deadly Rollick
rows.text: free with your commander out.

rows.name: Damn
rows.text: a removal spell early or a wrath late — and your board is mostly enchantments.

rows.name: Dauthi Voidwalker
rows.text: unblockable, blanks their graveyards, and steals their best card.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: taxes their first noncreature spell each turn.

rows.name: Deep Gnome Terramancer
rows.text: punishes every fetchland and every ramp spell at the table.

rows.name: Gleaming Splendor
rows.text: Treasures off their draws, and it can force draws itself.

rows.name: Demonic Tutor
rows.text: any card.

rows.name: Diabolic Intent
rows.text: any card for a spare body, and the sacrifice is on plan.

rows.name: Idyllic Tutor
rows.text: the enchantment half — Exquisite Blood, Enduring Tenacity, Moat or Ghostly Prison.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a wall and a mana source. The deck's clock is slow by design, so the losing pattern is being attacked to death on turn six, not running out of gas.

Do not protect Selenia forever. Her death trigger is a permanent Curse on an opponent, and Gift of Immortality turns that into one Curse per turn. Killing her on purpose is often the strongest line available.
Assemble the loop with Grand Abolisher up if you can. Two enchantments is a narrow window for the table to respond, and this deck has the mana to do both in one turn.

rows.name: Aetherflux Reservoir
rows.text: count your life before you go looking for the second combo piece. Fifty is closer than it looks with the gain doubled, and the Reservoir needs no partner.
